correctness.rationale: The six entrywise equations 2ad=2be=2cf=0, (a+b)u+(d+e)x=0, (b+c)v+(e+f)y=0, and (a+c)w+(d+f)z+xv+uy=0 are obtained by direct multiplication of arbitrary upper-triangular A,B. For odd characteristic, diagonal pairs lie in Ω={(s,t):st=0}, |Ω|=2q−1; splitting the endpoint diagonal states into U+W≠0 and W=−U, accounting for exceptional U=V=0 and U≠0,V=±U, gives the exact polynomial. The homogeneous bilinear constraint vanishes in ordinary W=−U cases because ad=be=0. In characteristic two, the diagonal restrictions disappear and the equalities among three k²-valued endpoint states partition all cases; the alternating determinant term vanishes when constrained vectors share a line. Independent symbolic expansion of both disjoint sums yields the claimed factors for arbitrary prime powers. An independently implemented six-by-six anticommutator rank census from the actual matrix-coefficient map gave q=2:928, q=3:7965, q=5:230625, q=7:1957501, with full rank spectra agreeing with the source log and with the earlier twisted-centralizer polynomial. Those finite checks are not a proof for all q; the full-field case partition is. No invertibility requirement, conjugacy quotient, or field-order interpolation is used; normalization q^12 is correct and includes q=2,3.

originality.rationale: The full 2026-10-25 twisted-centralizer result already computes the seven-term nullity distribution for AB=ωBA on the identical six-dimensional T3 and the identical odd-characteristic polynomial q^3(2q-1)(11q^2-15q+5). Its formal theorem excludes the symmetric twist ω=-1, so mere equality of displayed polynomials alone would not prove coverage. However the earlier proof explicitly states its resonance calculation uses only ω≠0,1; each diagonal-support case and pairwise resonance count indeed remains valid at ω=-1 in odd characteristic. The two-resonance constraints require ω≠1, not ω²≠1. Thus the already published full stratification proof specializes verbatim to anticommutation; q=3 is covered by the same algebraic argument even though the earlier nominal q≥4 condition arose from excluding ±1. Independent rank histograms for q=3,5,7 agree with all seven earlier strata. In characteristic two AB+BA=0 if and only if [A,B]=0; the full 2026-10-13 T3 commutator-fiber theorem already yields N_0=q^5(q^4+3q^3-2q^2-2q+1), and the 2026-11-02 full commutator theorem repeats the same zero fiber. The characteristic contrast and leading q-asymptotics are immediate consequences of those earlier two exact formulas. Therefore both branches and the submitted central quantitative claim are already implied by published mathematical proofs, despite exclusion of ω=-1 from the older twist theorem statement.

value.rationale: The ring T3 is indeed the natural first triangular algebra with nonzero radical square, and low-spectrum zero-Jordan-product probability is a mathematically motivated invariant. But both exact characteristic branches and their order-of-decay contrast are already immediate consequences of published complete stratified results: the odd branch from applying the October 25 twisted centralizer proof to -1, including its full rank spectrum, and the even branch from the October 13 zero Lie-commutator fiber. The assigned manuscript adds no distinct structural classification, nontrivial boundary, sharper invariant or motivatively independent fact beyond those prior formulas. q=3 and the characteristic dichotomy are direct specializations and elementary leading-term comparisons, not an independent contribution. The rejection concerns lack of new scientific value in this submission, not whether anticommuting probability itself is intrinsically worthwhile.

final_claim: For every prime power q and the full unital six-dimensional upper-triangular matrix algebra T3(F_q), the number N_q of ordered pairs of possibly singular matrices with AB+BA=0 equals q^3(2q−1)(11q²−15q+5) if char(F_q) is odd and q^5(q⁴+3q³−2q²−2q+1) if char(F_q)=2; the probability is N_q/q^12, asymptotic to 22 q^(−6) in growing odd fields and q^(−3) in characteristic-two extensions.
limitations: The result covers finite fields of any prime-power order and all upper triangular A,B, not invertible-only or nonzero-target anticommutators; the q=2,3,5,7 checks alone cannot certify all fields.

The closest earlier odd-twist statement excludes ω=-1, so rejection relies on inspecting and extending its full elementary proof. Exact rank spectra and case conditions, not identical polynomial text alone, support this conclusion.
The zero-Jordan-product article of Ghahramani and other unindexed specialized tables were not read in full; their absence would not negate the decisive earlier full mathematical implications.
